title: Selftest regression coverage for all nine fixes
description: Extend skills/logic-core/tests/selftest.sh with a regression case per fix: incompatible-bd shim falls back to TSV with a visible warning; merged branch stops inheriting tracking; audit and reconstruct of a non-checked-out branch use that branch's range; toggle non-current-branch messaging; TSV enrichment supersede; same-second TSV rows both survive; bogus 'commit deadbeef' evidence reported unresolved; conflicts exclude a planted unrelated worktree. Keep the suite exit-nonzero-on-failure and bash-3.2 clean.

title: reconstruct.sh: honor the requested branch instead of HEAD
description: reconstruct.sh only uses the branch argument for labels and external searches; commits, merge base, and changed files always come from HEAD. Reconstructing an unmerged feature from a main checkout yields an empty or wrong reconstruction. Fix: same treatment as audit.sh — verify the ref, derive range as merge-base(branch, base)..branch, and read files/commits from that range.

title: audit.sh: honor the requested branch instead of HEAD
description: audit.sh computes merge-base and diff from HEAD even when a branch argument names a different branch, so evidence on an unmerged target is reported unresolved and coverage gaps come from the wrong diff. Fix: resolve the supplied branch to a ref (verify it exists; error clearly if not), use merge-base <branch> <base> and diff <mb>..<branch>, and run the sha reachability checks with merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> <branch>.

title: Exclude merged branches from ancestor inheritance
description: lib.sh logic_effective_state step 3: after an enabled feature branch merges to main, its tip is an ancestor of main, so main (and every later branch) resolves as tracked with the old feature as logical branch. Fix: skip an ancestor candidate when it is itself an ancestor of the repo default base (origin/main, main, origin/master, master) — i.e. already merged. A derived, unmerged worktree branch keeps inheriting. Add a selftest case: enable feature, merge to main, assert main resolves off; assert an unmerged derived branch still resolves on.

title: bd capability probe + loud TSV fallback
description: lib.sh logic_log_row and every bd reader assume the modern bd API. With ~/.local/bin/bd v0.49.1 (no query/metadata/decision-type), writes fail silently inside the post-commit hook and reads return empty. Fix: probe capabilities once (e.g. bd query --help and bd create --help grep, cached in .logic/), and on incompatible-or-failing bd, fall back to the TSV backend IN THE SAME CALL and surface a one-line warning (stderr for interactive scripts; a .logic/WARNINGS file the SessionStart hook can echo for hooks). Silent loss is the failure mode being eliminated; a wrong backend choice must always leave a visible trace. Verified live: login shells on this machine resolve the old binary.

title: logic: Codex review remediation (PR #2)
description:
Fix the 9 findings from the Codex review of branch angus/logic-decision-trail (https://github.com/gpu-cli/skills/pull/2). All 9 were verified real; none dismissed.

Key empirical confirmation for finding 1: this machine has TWO bd binaries — ~/.local/bin/bd v0.49.1 (login-shell PATH winner; no 'bd query', no --metadata, no --type=decision) and /opt/homebrew/bin/bd v0.62.0 (non-login PATH winner; full API). The git post-commit hook inherits the committer's environment, so capture silently fails whenever the old binary wins PATH. The suite must probe capabilities and fall back to TSV loudly, never silently.

Finding groups:
- Scoping correctness: audit.sh, reconstruct.sh, conflicts.sh derive ranges/streams from HEAD or all worktrees instead of the requested branch.
- Tracking resolution: merged-branch ancestor inheritance wrongly tracks main; toggle for a non-current branch claims effect it does not have.
- Backend robustness: bd capability detection, TSV enrichment, TSV row identity.
- Audit integrity: 'commit <sha>' evidence auto-resolves without validation.
notes: IMPLEMENTED in commit bc5ebab on angus/logic-decision-trail (PR #2). All 9 findings fixed + regression coverage; selftest 33/33 with a negative control proving the new cases fail against pre-fix code. Confirmed live: ~/.local/bin/bd v0.49.1 wins login-shell PATH and lacks bd query/--metadata/decision, which is why capture failed silently.

title: Real-branch trial in virgil
description: Enable tracking on an active virgil branch, run genuine multi-agent work including at least one parallel worktree, exercise /show-logic end to end (tables, audit, conflicts, --pr on a draft PR), and fix the friction found. Exit criteria: a reviewer who was not present can reconstruct the why of the branch from /show-logic output alone.
notes: REMAINING: real-branch trial in virgil is genuine follow-up — needs live multi-agent work in the virgil repo. A synthetic selftest (skills/logic-core/tests/selftest.sh, 16/16) proves the mechanical core; the human-in-the-loop trial is intentionally left open.

title: Write README and usage docs
description: Three commands, the row lifecycle (stub, enrich, promote, expire), the three-layer compliance model, the storage matrix (beads default, TSV fallback), reconstruction caveats and the inferred-row warning, worktree reconciliation behavior, and the install story for a consumer repo.

title: Phase 6: docs, real-branch trial, v2 backlog
description: Make the suite adoptable: document it, prove it on a real branch in virgil, and record the deliberately deferred scope.

title: Implement the gc pass
description: Opportunistic cleanup when /show-logic runs: promoted decision rows whose logical branch was deleted without merging get compacted or closed; rows for merged branches are kept as mainline history; wisp stubs need nothing, TTL handles them. Detection via git branch --merged and reflog. Never touches rows for live branches.

title: Implement PR push (--pr)
description: Compose a Rationale section from the rendered trail and write it into the PR description via gh pr edit, wrapped in HTML comment markers so a re-run replaces the section idempotently instead of stacking copies. When the trail includes inferred rows, the section embeds the reconstruction warning verbatim.

title: Implement the cross-model review step
description: A subagent on a different model family reads the trail and the diff, then flags weak or absent evidence, verification claimed without proof, and risky calls (premature, scope-creeping, symptom-papering). Mandatory whenever the trail contains inferred rows and before any PR push; best-effort otherwise. Output is an Attention section naming the reviewer model.

title: Implement conflict detection between parallel streams
description: Tier 1: evidence or territory overlap between rows from different worktrees (mechanical). Tier 2: git merge-tree between derived branches finds real textual conflicts, mapped to the decision rows whose evidence touches conflicted paths (mechanical). Tiers 1 and 2 feed tier 3: the model judges the paired rows for semantic contradiction and writes a one-line tension note. A clean section reads none detected, not none exist.

title: Implement reconstruction mode
description: Three detection states with distinct messages: tracking was off (full reconstruction behind a warning banner), tracking started partway (real rows plus reconstruction of the untracked span only), tracking on but zero rows (compliance failure called out, likely hook breakage). Inference sources in reliability order: commit messages and trailers, diff grouped into logical units, beads task issues referencing the branch, PR description and comments. Inferred rows carry actor=inferred with hypothesis phrasing (likely because X). Strictly a view: nothing is written back to beads.

title: Implement the git-evidence audit
description: Every row's evidence must resolve: a SHA within the branch range, a file:line present in the diff, an artifact path that exists. Rows that fail get flagged, not dropped. Substantive diff regions with no covering row are reported as gaps. This replaces the Cursor original's transcript audit with an artifact that always exists.

title: Implement terminal rendering
description: Default output: one table per stream (worktree or actor), headed by worktree path, literal branch, and actors, main checkout first. Flag pending-user-note rows and unenriched stubs distinctly. Render column -t friendly with a markdown option.

title: Phase 5: show-logic skill (read path, reconstruction, reconciliation)
description: The read side: collect, audit, render in the terminal, reconstruct when tracking was off, reconcile parallel worktrees, review cross-model, optionally push to the PR.

title: Implement collection and merge
description: Per the Phase 1 visibility spike: either one label query against the shared Dolt server, or a sweep of git worktree list --porcelain running bd query --json in each worktree, deduped by issue ID. Merge in TSV-fallback rows if present. Order by timestamp. Output a normalized row list the rest of the skill consumes.

title: Compliance end-to-end test
description: Prove the floor: a human commit and an agent commit on a tracked branch both produce stubs, including from a secondary worktree; enrichment promotes stubs to permanent decision beads; unpromoted stubs expire via TTL; an untracked branch produces nothing and pays no observable latency.

title: Implement SessionStart orientation injection
description: One line when tracking is active for the current checkout: the logical branch, the storage backend, and a pointer to the track-logic skill for the row protocol. Orientation, not enforcement; keep it to a single line mirroring the beads hook pattern.

title: Implement .githooks/post-commit stub script
description: On every commit to a tracked branch, mechanically create an ephemeral wisp stub row: evidence is the SHA, decision is the commit subject, actor is the committer, why is empty. Fast no-op when tracking is off for the resolved logical branch. Degrades silently when bd is missing (TSV stub or skip). Must never break or slow a commit, human or agent, in any worktree.

title: Implement the Stop hook enrichment gate
description: When the turn touched a tracked branch and left unenriched stubs: block completion once with a specific instruction to promote and explain the stubs that represent real decisions and leave trivial ones to expire. Guard with stop_hook_active so it fires once and never loops. Legitimate mechanical-only turns state that and finish.

title: Phase 4: compliance layer (mechanical capture plus turn-boundary gate)
description: Three-layer enforcement so no layer depends on the model remembering an instruction: capture by construction (post-commit stubs), enrichment at the turn boundary (Stop hook), audit at read time (Phase 5). Session-start injection is orientation only.

title: Wire enable to install compliance hooks
description: On enable: set core.hooksPath to the committed .githooks directory (covers all worktrees via shared repo config), verify bd availability and warn if falling back to TSV, print what was installed. On disable: hooks stay installed but no-op fast; document why (other branches may still be tracked).

title: Implement the toggle command
description: /toggle-track-logic with no argument flips the current state; optional on or off sets it explicitly; optional branch argument targets a branch other than the current one. Always ends by printing the resulting state and its scope (which branch, which storage) so a silent flip on the wrong branch cannot happen.

title: Implement ancestry-based branch resolution
description: Shared helper that resolves the logical branch for the current checkout: exact config match, then glob, then check whether any enabled branch is an ancestor of HEAD via git merge-base --is-ancestor (covers derived worktree branches forked from an enabled feature branch). Returns the logical branch name that rows get labeled with. Used by both hooks and the log helper.

title: Define config.json schema and precedence
description: Schema: { default: on|off, branches: { exact or glob: on|off }, storage: beads|tsv, storageOverrides: { branch: beads|tsv } }. Precedence: exact match, then glob, then default. The file is committed and the copy in the current checkout governs, so enabling for a branch happens on that branch. Document toggle dirt as intended behavior: the config change appears in the PR diff and shows tracking was on.

title: Phase 3: toggle-track-logic skill (config and toggle)
description: The thin config editor: per-project default, per-branch overrides, storage selection, and the enable-time installation of the compliance hooks.

title: Specify agent-prompted capture rules
description: When a decision is genuinely the user's (approach picked, suggestion rejected, scope call) and the why is unstated: interactive sessions ask for one line via AskUserQuestion and log it attributed to the user; background sessions log the pending-user-note placeholder and never block. /show-logic surfaces pending rows for annotation.

title: Implement TSV fallback backend
description: Per-writer files at .audit/<logical-branch>/<actor>.tsv (one log per writer, no merge conflicts). Activated by storage config override or automatically when bd is unavailable (CI, collaborators without beads). /show-logic merges TSV rows with bd rows at read time.

title: Implement /track-logic manual entry
description: The user-facing command for direct decision capture: /track-logic "kept Metal because Canvas dropped frames". Appends a user-attributed row via the helper and echoes the written row back so the user sees exactly what was recorded.

title: Implement the log helper script
description: Single entrypoint used by agents, the post-commit hook, and manual entry. Stamps ts, resolves the logical branch (via the ancestry helper from Phase 3), routes to bd or TSV per config, strips stray tabs and newlines, and prefixes cells starting with formula bytes (=, +, -, @) for the TSV backend so spreadsheet opens are safe. Must be callable from a bare shell with no session context.

title: Implement bd storage mapping
description: Map a row to a decision-type bead: title is the decision, description is the why, label logic:<logical-branch> scopes it, metadata JSON carries actor, phase, evidence, result, git_branch, worktree. Define the query patterns /show-logic will use (bd query type=decision AND label=logic:<branch>). Confirm decision-type beads stay out of bd ready and task views.

title: Write SKILL.md: the row protocol
description: Define the row: ts, actor, phase, decision, why, evidence, result, plus git_branch and worktree in metadata. Rules carried from the Cursor original: log decision points and checkpoints rather than every action; one line per cell; plain language, no AI-speak; evidence is a pointer (SHA, file:line, artifact path), never prose; append-only, a wrong call gets a superseding row. New rules: every row carries an actor; unattended sessions never block on a human, they log why=pending-user-note and move on.

title: Phase 2: track-logic skill (row protocol and storage)
description: The core skill: what a decision row is, how it is written, and where it goes. Both hooks and /show-logic reference this skill so the format lives in exactly one place.

title: Decide packaging and install story
description: Fix the layout: three skill dirs (track-logic, toggle-track-logic, show-logic) in this skills repo, where shared scripts live, where config.json lives (inside toggle-track-logic, the skill that edits it), and how a consumer repo like virgil installs the suite (symlink into .claude/skills per existing convention, .githooks directory committed in the consumer repo). Write the layout decision in notes.
notes: DECISION: 4 skill dirs — logic-core (non-invocable engine: lib + all scripts + hook sources + refs), track-logic, toggle-track-logic, show-logic (thin, user-invocable, call the engine). Per-repo runtime state lives in committed .logic/. Interactive scripts run from the installed skill; hooks run from materialized .logic/ copies so they survive worktrees.

title: Spike: hook wiring (SessionStart, Stop gate, core.hooksPath)
description: Verify three harness mechanisms: (1) SessionStart injection mirroring the existing beads hook pattern; (2) a Stop hook that blocks completion once with an instruction, guarded by stop_hook_active so it never loops; (3) core.hooksPath applying to every worktree of the repo, with a fast no-op path so untracked branches pay nothing. Record the exact settings.json hook config in notes.
notes: FINDING: consumer installs put skills in .agents/skills (GITIGNORED) and .claude (GITIGNORED), so skill files are absent from git worktrees. DECISION: runtime must live in a COMMITTED .logic/ dir at repo root (config.json, runtime/logic.sh, githooks/post-commit, hooks/*). install-hooks sets core.hooksPath=.logic/githooks (relative, resolves per-worktree). Git post-commit hook is the robust Layer-1 capture; Claude Stop/SessionStart hooks (.claude/settings.json) are best-effort Layer-2 for interactive sessions.

title: Spike: wisp lifecycle mechanics (ephemeral create, TTL, promote)
description: Verify from a plain shell script: creating an ephemeral/wisp bead non-interactively (as a git post-commit hook would), how TTL compaction is configured and when unpromoted wisps actually expire, and the exact semantics of bd promote (wisp to permanent decision bead, preserving metadata). Record the exact commands and TTL config in notes. Blocks the post-commit stub script.
notes: FINDING: compaction_enabled=false and auto_compact_enabled=false in this repo, so ephemeral wisp TTL expiry is NOT reliable. --ephemeral creates skills-wisp-* but they would accumulate. DECISION: skip wisps; use regular decision beads created-then-closed with a 'logic-stub' lifecycle label; cleanup is explicit via gc.sh. Repos with compaction on can opt into wisps later. Also: decision beads DO appear in bd ready unless closed, so log-decision closes each row immediately.

title: Spike: beads visibility across worktrees
description: Determine whether bd here runs against a shared Dolt server per repo (rows from every worktree visible instantly) or per-checkout state that converges through git merges. The answer decides the /show-logic collection strategy: a single label query vs a sweep (git worktree list --porcelain, then bd query --json inside each worktree, dedupe by issue ID). End with the chosen strategy written in this issue's notes.
notes: FINDING: beads uses a shared Dolt SQL server (per-repo dolt sql-server process); bd walks up dirs to find .beads. Worktrees under .claude/worktrees/ resolve to the parent repo's .beads, so all rows are visible from one 'bd query' regardless of worktree. STRATEGY: /show-logic default = single label query; worktree-sweep only as fallback for no-db/JSONL collaborators.

title: Phase 1: Foundations and verification spikes
description: Resolve the design unknowns that shape later phases before writing any skill text. Each spike ends with a short written answer in the issue notes.

title: logic: decision-trail skill suite (/track-logic, /toggle-track-logic, /show-logic)
description:
Build a three-command skill suite that keeps a reviewable decision trail for branches worked on by multiple agents and the user, adapted from Cursor's show-me-your-work skill (TSV decision log) to a beads-native, multi-agent, PR-oriented design.

Core design (agreed 2026-07-23):
- Storage: beads decision-type issues by default (label logic:<branch>, metadata {actor, phase, evidence, result, git_branch, worktree}); per-writer TSV files under .audit/<branch>/ as escape hatch and auto-fallback when bd is unavailable.
- Toggle: /toggle-track-logic edits a committed config.json in the skill dir (project default + per-branch globs + storage overrides, precedence exact > glob > default). Ancestry resolution: a worktree branch derived from an enabled branch is tracked, rows labeled with the logical branch.
- Capture compliance (three layers): (1) git post-commit hook via core.hooksPath creates ephemeral wisp stub rows mechanically for every commit, agent or human, across all worktrees; (2) Stop hook blocks once per turn to promote/enrich stubs that represent real decisions (stop_hook_active guard); (3) read-time audit in /show-logic. Session-start injection is orientation only, not enforcement.
- User decisions: actor column on every row, agent-prompted one-liners via AskUserQuestion when interactive, pending-user-note placeholders when unattended, /track-logic 'reason' for direct manual entry.
- /show-logic: terminal table by default; git-evidence audit; reconstruction mode for untracked branches (3 states: off / partial / on-but-empty; inferred rows marked actor=inferred behind a warning banner, no silent backfill); worktree reconciliation with per-stream tables and 3-tier conflict detection (evidence overlap + git merge-tree feeding model-judged contradictions); mandatory cross-model review for inferred trails; --pr pushes an idempotent Rationale section into the PR description.
- Cleanup: unpromoted wisps expire via TTL; gc pass compacts promoted rows of deleted-unmerged branches; merged branches keep rows as mainline history.

Origin: https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/3fe2823c/pstack/skills/show-me-your-work/SKILL.md
notes: IMPLEMENTED on branch angus/logic-decision-trail; draft PR https://github.com/gpu-cli/skills/pull/2. Phases 2-6.1 + 6.3 closed. Open: 6.2 (real virgil trial) and 6.7/6.8/6.9 v2 backlog. selftest 16/16.

description: Validate the skill against a real repo with agent-written comments: run /correct-comments on a diff and on a directory, confirm comment-only edits (no behavior change), confirm agent/bead references are stripped and kept comments read as one-line STE-100 English. Add the skill to skills-lock.json / repo registry per existing conventions, update the repo README skill list, and run skill-shield over the new skill before merging.

title: Write SKILL.md with comment rules and cleanup workflow
description: Author skills/clean-comments/SKILL.md following the layout of existing skills in this repo (see skills/logic, skills/skill-shield). Encode the full ruleset from the epic design notes: necessity test, one-line max, agent-reference and bead-reference removal, TODO/FIXME/HACK notations, ASD-STE100 simplified technical english (reference: https://github.com/danyuchn/asd-ste100-skill), and the nine comment-quality rules. Define scope behavior: diff-only by default, path or repo-wide when explicitly requested. Hard constraint: comment-only edits, never touch executable code, preserve linter/formatter/generated-code directives.

title: Add /correct-comments command
description: Add the user-invocable command surface for the skill: /correct-comments [path]. No arguments cleans the current diff; a path argument cleans that file or directory; an explicit flag or 'all' cleans the repo. Command reports a summary of removals/rewrites grouped by rule so the user can review before committing. Decide and document whether this is a command file in the skill or a section of SKILL.md, matching repo conventions.

title: Add agentic-file guidance injection (prevention)
description: Install step that appends a short comment-management note to the user's agentic files (CLAUDE.md and/or AGENTS.md): the write-time rules that prevent verbose commentary from being written at all. Must be idempotent (detect an existing note and update rather than duplicate) and ask before writing to files the skill did not create. This is the highest-leverage deliverable per the validation research.

title: clean-comments: skill to clean up agentic code commentary
description: Add an installable skill at skills/clean-comments that reduces verbose agentic commentary in codebases. Scope was validated against existing solutions (motlin comment-cleanup, various de-slop skills): our differentiators are ASD-STE100 plain-English rewriting of kept comments, CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md guidance injection for prevention, and removal of agent self-references and bead/issue-tracker references. Deliverables: (1) SKILL.md encoding the comment rules; (2) a /correct-comments command that cleans a project or specified path, diff-scoped by default; (3) an install step that appends a comment-management note to the user's agentic files; (4) optional CI/PR flag-only check (explicitly NOT a blocking pre-commit rewrite).
design: Comment rules to encode: necessity test (delete if clear without it); one line max in almost all cases; strip agent self-references and bead/issue references when the tracker is not shared; use standard notations (TODO/FIXME/HACK) for incomplete or dependent work; ASD-STE100 simplified technical English for kept comments; and the nine rules: no duplicating code, no excusing unclear code, unclear comment implies unclear code, dispel confusion, explain unidiomatic code, link source of copied code, link external references where most helpful, comment bug fixes, mark incomplete implementations. Cleanup is comment-only — never change executable code. Prevention (guidance note) is the highest-leverage piece; hook rewrites at commit time were considered and rejected.

title: Add confidence and decision-quality review to logic trails
description: Extend the logic decision row with coarse perceived confidence, preserve backward compatibility across beads and TSV, render the confidence column, and add a separate choice-quality review section for evidence fit, assumptions, risks, counterexamples, and owner rulings.
notes: Implemented coarse perceived confidence (high/medium/low/unknown) across Beads metadata and backward-compatible TSV rows; added table rendering, capture/enrichment guidance, and a separate Decision quality assessment for evidence fit, assumptions, boundary cases, contradictions, and owner rulings. Forward-test caught and fixed TSV branch normalization. Validation: 43/43 self-tests, bash -n, ShellCheck, git diff --check, and isolated forward-test all pass. PR: https://github.com/gpu-cli/skills/pull/3. Generic quick_validate remains incompatible with this repo's pre-existing argument-hint/user-invocable frontmatter keys.
close_reason: Implemented and validated in commit c093bd7

title: conflicts.sh: restrict streams to trail participants
description: Tier-2 merge-tree pairs are built from every checked-out worktree regardless of the requested branch, so /show-logic feature-a can report conflicts between unrelated feature-b and feature-c. Fix: filter streams to worktrees that participate in the trail — worktrees appearing in the collected rows, plus worktrees whose branch has the logical branch as ancestor (unmerged). Tier-1 already implicitly filters via rows; make tier-2 match.

title: audit.sh: validate 'commit <sha>' evidence instead of auto-resolving
description: The evidence check accepts any string starting with 'commit ' as resolved without verifying the commit exists or is in the branch, so fabricated evidence yields the reassuring all-rows-resolve output — defeating the audit. Fix: parse the sha token, require git cat-file -e and merge-base --is-ancestor against the audited branch; unparseable or unreachable pointers are reported as unresolved.

title: TSV row identity: survive same-second rows
description: collect.sh builds the TSV row id from ts+actor+sha; two manual rows by the same actor in the same second (empty sha) collide and unique_by drops one silently. Fix: include a content component in the id (e.g. cksum of decision+why) or write a per-row nonce column at log time. Interacts with the enrichment supersede logic from the TSV-enrichment task — land them together and dedupe deliberately: identical-content duplicates collapse, distinct decisions never do.

title: TSV backend: support stub enrichment via supersede rows
description: logic_find_stub_by_sha and logic_enrich are bd-only, so on the TSV fallback a captured stub can never be enriched even though the skills instruct users to enrich stubs. Fix with append-only semantics: log.sh --enrich <sha> on TSV appends a new enriched row carrying the same sha, and collect.sh dedupes per-sha preferring the non-stub row (supersede, never rewrite). Update track-logic SKILL.md wording so enrichment guidance matches both backends.

title: toggle.sh: fix non-current-branch semantics
description: toggle.sh on other-branch edits the CURRENT checkout's .logic/config.json (uncommitted, on the current branch) and prints that tracking takes effect on the target branch — it does not: the target worktree/branch never sees the config and its post-commit hook no-ops. Decide and implement one: (a) locate the target branch's worktree via git worktree list and install/edit there, or (b) simpler and honest — keep the edit local but replace the misleading message with explicit instructions that the config change must be committed to the target branch to take effect, and detect+warn when the target branch is checked out in another worktree. Option (b) is the recommended scope.

title: Optional CI/PR flag-only comment check
description: Optional, non-blocking check for CI or PR review that flags rule-violating comments without rewriting them. Explicitly not a pre-commit rewrite hook: an LLM pass at commit time is slow, non-deterministic, and edits already-reviewed code. Could be a GitHub Action comment or a prompt for /review. Evaluate whether this earns its keep; fine to close as wontfix if the guidance note plus manual command proves sufficient.
